predecessors.note: Ceuta is the Marinid hand-over; the later enclaves came from the Wattasids, Marinid remnants and local principalities (see the ledger counterparts).

land.text: Mazagan (El Jadida), the last Portuguese foothold, evacuated 10 March 1769

successors.note: Earlier hand-overs: Agadir, Safi, Azemmour, Mehdya (1541) and Ksar es-Seghir and Asilah (1550) to the Saadis; Asilah (1589) and Ceuta (1640) to Spain; Tangier (1661) to England; Casablanca (1755) to Morocco.

capitals.name: Ceuta

capitals.name: Mazagan (El Jadida)

ledger.note: 21 August 1415: Portugal takes Ceuta. The Portuguese conquered Ceuta 'on 21 August 1415' 'from the Marinid Sultanate'; Pedro de Meneses holds it against the Marinid and Granadan siege of 1419.
1458: Portugal takes Ksar es-Seghir (Alcacer-Ceguer). 'the taking of Ksar es-Seghir (1458), Arzila and Tangier (1471)'. The Marinid dossier records the loss; the pages opened do not name the holder.

1471: Portugal takes Arzila and Tangier. Arzila 'conquered in 1471'; Tangier held 1471-1661 (the Marinid dossier has Afonso V take Tangier in 1465 and the conflicts page says it was 'won and lost several times between 1460 and 1464'). Holder not named on the pages.

1488: Portugal holds Safi. The enclaves list gives Safi 1488-1541; the pages opened name no previous holder (southern Morocco was a set of principalities under the Wattasids), so the land is entered as nobody's.

region.text: Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue (Agadir)

ledger.note: 1505: Portugal founds Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue at Agadir. 'Agadir (Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue): Founded in 1505-06'; the enclaves list has 1505-1541. No holder named.
1513: Portugal holds Azemmour. 'Azemmour (Azamor): 1513-1541' (both lists); no previous holder named.
1514: Portugal founds Mazagan. 'Mazagan (El Jadida): Founded in 1514-17' (conflicts page); the enclaves list says 'seized 1486', a conflict not resolved here. Held until 1769.

region.text: Casablanca (Anfa) and Mehdya (Sao Joao da Mamora)

ledger.note: 1515: Portugal takes Mehdya and Casablanca. 'Mehdya: taken 1515; lost 1541' and 'Casablanca (Anfa/Casa Branca): 1515-1755'.
1541: Mehdya is lost. 'Mehdya: taken 1515; lost 1541'; the page does not name the taker (the Saadi dossier records the 1614 Spanish capture of La Mamora from Fez).

region.text: Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue (Agadir)

ledger.note: September 1541: Agadir falls to the Saadis. The infobox dates the fall of Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue to 'March-September 1541'; the six-month siege ended with the governor's surrender to Muhammad al-Shaykh.
October 1541: the Portuguese evacuate Safi and Azemmour. 'the ports of Safi and Azammur were evacuated by the Portuguese in October 1541'.
1550: the Portuguese leave Ksar es-Seghir and Asilah. Ksar es-Seghir 1458-1550 and Asilah 1471-1550 (enclaves list); the conflicts page has Ksar es-Seghir abandoned in 1549 and Arzila in 1550.
1577: Portugal retakes Asilah. 'Asilah (Arzila/Arcila): 1471-1550; retaken 1577, lost 1589'; the enclaves list; Alcacer Quibir followed on 4 August 1578.
1589: Asilah is lost. 'retaken 1577, lost 1589'; the Saadi dossier has it go to Spain in 1589 (Portugal was under the Spanish crown from 1580).

1640: Ceuta stays with Spain. 'Ceuta: taken 1415; held to 1640, when it stayed with Spain. Spanish possession acknowledged in the Treaty of Lisbon (1668).' The Ceuta conquest page says it 'remained under Portuguese control until it was transferred to Spain in 1668'.
1661: Tangier is ceded to England. 'Tangier was ceded to King Charles II in 1661' (enclaves: English 1661-1684).
1755: Casablanca is abandoned. 'Casablanca (Anfa/Casa Branca): 1515-1755; abandoned after the 1755 Lisbon earthquake'.

10 March 1769: Portugal evacuates Mazagan, its last foothold in Morocco. 'El Jadida (Mazagan/Mazagao): seized 1486; evacuated 10 March 1769'; 'The Portuguese evacuated Mazagan in 1769' (conflicts page).

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Ceuta
wars.outcome: Portugal took Ceuta on 21 August 1415 from the Marinid Sultanate; the Marinid sultan Abu Said Uthman III sent no aid.

wars.name: Marinid siege of Ceuta
wars.outcome: 'Abu Said Uthman III laid siege to Ceuta with the help of the Nasrid Emir of Granada Muhammad VIII'; the Portuguese repulsed it.
wars.note: The page dates the siege to 1419, not 1418.

wars.name: Portuguese expansion in Morocco
wars.outcome: Ksar es-Seghir in 1458, Arzila and Tangier in 1471, Safi from 1488, Agadir 1505-06, Azemmour 1513, Mazagan 1514-17, Casablanca and Mehdya 1515; the conflicts page lists the Wattasid Sultanate as a belligerent from 1472 to 1554.

wars.name: Fall of Agadir and the Saadi campaign of 1541
wars.outcome: Muhammad al-Shaykh besieged Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue for six months (March-September 1541); the Portuguese then evacuated Safi and Azemmour in October. 'Only Ceuta, Tangier and Mazagan remained in Portuguese hands' besides the northern posts.

wars.name: Battle of Alcacer Quibir (Ksar el-Kebir)
wars.outcome: Fought 'on 4 August 1578'; no territorial change is on the pages opened for Portuguese Morocco.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War and Ceuta
wars.outcome: Ceuta stayed with Spain in 1640 and was acknowledged Spanish in the Treaty of Lisbon (1668).
wars.note: The Ceuta conquest page: 'remained under Portuguese control until it was transferred to Spain in 1668'.

wars.name: Moroccan reconquest of Mazagan
wars.outcome: The Portuguese evacuated Mazagan on 10 March 1769; a Peace and Friendship Agreement followed in 1774.

certainty.note: Fortified towns held by garrisons: the walls are the territory; no hinterland frontier exists on the pages, and the 25 km circles are about the grid minimum for a coastal town.

notes: Cliopatria has no 'Portuguese Morocco' row; the Cliopatria row 'Portuguese Africa' (1507-1581, max 35,685 km2, af-08) is a different bounding of the same coast and its years overlap this dossier's keyframes 1507-1581: the integrator should choose one of the two for those years. Wikipedia has no article of this exact title among the pages opened (null). The enclaves list and the conflicts page disagree on: Mazagan (seized 1486 vs founded 1514-17), Ksar es-Seghir's end (1549 vs 1550), Mogador (1506-1525 vs 1506-1510) and Aguz (1506-1525 vs 1520-25); Mogador and Aguz are short-lived and not entered. The first conquests (Ksar es-Seghir 1458, Arzila and Tangier 1471) name no holder on the pages opened; the Marinid dossier records them as losses, so 'marinid-sultanate' is the counterpart at confidence 2, and the later gains (Safi, Agadir, Azemmour, Mazagan, Casablanca, Mehdya) are entered against 'nobody'. Ceuta: 1640 (enclaves) vs 1668 (Ceuta page). The Spanish capture of Asilah in 1589 is the Saadi dossier's reading. Gazetteer names needed: Asilah, Ksar es-Seghir, Azemmour, Mehdya and Essaouira as places (coordinates stand in).
